reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing behaviour: the cited paragraphs show only cause-based exits (9.3) across a three-year term with an express no-termination take-or-pay commitment (2.1), which the rule flags as a deviation for terms longer than 12 months.

The inserted Section 9.4 tracks the preferred position and model language closely: 30 days' written notice, in whole or in part, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee or accelerated Fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a term.

The 'notwithstanding Section 2.1' carve-out is a proportionate, targeted addition needed to make the convenience right effective against the take-or-pay language rather than an unnecessary rewrite of Section 2.1.

The edit is additive and leaves existing termination rights intact, i.e., the smallest change that reaches the playbook position; deterministic checks confirm the Customer convenience right is present.

The comment accurately describes what changed and why, cites the playbook gap, and offers the 60-90 day / three-month fee cap fallback in the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
